3. The Respondent No. 2 entered appearance and denied all these allegations made in the election petition by filing a written statement before the Tribunal. It was stated by Respondent No. 2 that the election was held in peaceful atmosphere and no illegality or irregularity was committed in the election; as such the election petition was liable to be dismissed. 

 10. As to the third contention of Mr. Hyder, we find that the Rules specifically provide that the deposit is to be made under a specific head of the treasury chalan i.e. under "Deposits and Advances-part-II-Deposits in connection with Elections", but in the present case the deposit has been Made not under this specific 'Head' but has been made in the High Court Form No. A-1 which is meant for civil deposits in connection with civil cases. Of course, in this Form it was stated that the deposit was to be credited to the Returning Officer of the said Election, but instead of mentioning the appropriate "Head" as provided in Rule 15(5) a wrong Rule i.e. Rule 64 of the Rules has been mentioned. Deposit under Rule 64 relates to a different matter. Though the money ultimately went in to the treasury, it would not be possible for the Tribunal to trace it out and connect the same with the case before it. The Election Tribunal got no power to pass any order in respect of any deposit made in the civil court, though the Munsif acts as the Election Tribunal. 

 11. Mr. Nizamuddin Ryder has next contended that Rule 59 does not provide that for want of deposit or wrong deposit an election petition shall be dismissed. He has tried to draw an analogy between deposits made in pre-emption eases under the Bengal Tenancy Act, 1885 and the State Acquisition Act, 1950 and the deposits made under the Election Rules. He has argued that in the former there are specific provisions for dismissal of pre-emption cases in absence of deposits. This analogy, we find, is not applicable in Election cases simply because the deposits in pre-emption-cases are required for setting aside sales of land for transfer of the same to the pre-emptor.
